rationale: C16 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child’s central import-control machinery. Both directives make entry or withdrawal for consumption contingent on a license issued under a cabinet secretary’s regulations, require licenses to conform to allocated quantitative limits, and direct equitable allocation of quotas. The child substantially expands and adapts that framework to petroleum, geographic districts, multiple product classes, appeals, and national-security findings. C05 is highly relevant to the petroleum program and is expressly revoked by the child, but it functions more as the policy regime being replaced than as the strongest textual template. C14 contains similar licensed supplemental-quota machinery but is narrower and less closely parallel than C16.

shared_material.child_excerpt: no crude oil or unfinished oils may be entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption ... except (1) by or for the account of a person to whom a license has been issued by the Secretary of the Interior pursuant to an allocation ... in accordance with regulations issued by the Secretary, and such entries and withdrawals may be made only in accordance with the terms of such license
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Articles included in Lists I and II ... shall be permitted to be entered only by or for the account of a person or firm to whom a license has been issued by or under the authority of the Secretary of Agriculture, and only in accordance with the terms of such license.
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, materially shared operative language establishing the same license-based gate for imports, adapted from agricultural products to petroleum.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Such regulations shall ... provide for a system of allocation of the authorized imports ... and for the issuance of licenses pursuant to such system
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Such licenses shall be issued under regulations of the Secretary of Agriculture which he determines will ... result in (1) the equitable distribution of the respective quotas for such articles among importers or users
shared_material.explanation: Both use secretary-issued regulations to connect quantitative import ceilings, allocations among importers or users, and individual licenses.

shared_material.child_excerpt: such regulations shall provide, to the extent possible, for a fair and equitable distribution among persons having refinery capacity
shared_material.parent_excerpt: regulations ... will, to the fullest extent practicable, result in ... the equitable distribution of the respective quotas for such articles among importers or users
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the parent’s equitable-distribution standard to refinery operators.

shared_material.child_excerpt: no department, establishment, or agency of the United States shall import finished products in excess of the respective allocations made to them
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The provisions of this proclamation shall not apply to articles imported by or for the account of any department or agency of the Government of the United States.
shared_material.explanation: Both separately address federal-agency imports within the licensing and quota scheme, though the child replaces the complete exemption with allocation limits.
